title: USMNT’s Sergiño Dest salvages draw for PSV with goal in Champions League opener
content:
Sergiño Dest carried his hot start to the season with PSV Eindhoven into the Champions League, salvaging a point for his Dutch club in a 1-1 draw against Shakhtar Donetsk.

Dest, who has had two goals and two assists in PSV’s first four Eredivisie games of the season, scored the equalizer three minutes into the second half with a clinical finish from inside the Shakhtar box. Armando Obispo had cut back a cross into space at the top of the box, and an eager Dest was the first to get to it, rifling a right-footed finisher into the back of the net to make it 1-1.

The goal was Dest’s second career goal in the Champions League, with the first coming in 2023 for Barcelona against another Ukrainian opponent, Dynamo Kyiv.

It was a bit of a just reward for Dest, who appeared to have been fouled in the build-up to Shakhtar’s opening goal in first-half stoppage time, but no call was given. He took a crunching tackle in the center circle while attempting to recover possession off his own heavy touch, but Shakhtar capitalized as he remained on the ground, attacking the space at right back where he would have otherwise been defending to score the goal.

The Champions League this season is largely devoid of the USMNT’s top talent, with most of the core’s clubs participating in the UEFA Europa League. PSV, with Dest and Ricardo Pepi, has become the must-watch side for any U.S. fan monitoring the competition. Pepi, who has three goals in five league games so far this season, started and played 83 minutes on Thursday.

Beyond the PSV tandem, teen star Mathis Albert (Borussia Dortmund), Johnny Cardoso (Atlético Madrid), Alex Freeman (Villarreal) and the Austria-based duo of George Bello and Sam Adeniran (LASK) make up the remainder of U.S. internationals competing in the League Phase.

As for the goalscorer Dest, he is a top candidate to be included on the first post-World Cup roster that Mauricio Pochettino is due to announce next week. He started four of the USMNT’s five games during the World Cup, though he was taken off at halftime of the round-of-16 defeat to Belgium.
